Standard: The air vehicle structure and components can withstand the loads spectrum and AR aerodynamic environment (e.g., temperature, vibration, duration) generated between itself and the targeted tanker/receiver air vehicle(s) throughout the AR envelope over the DSL of the air vehicle. Life-limited parts are identified and replacement intervals (e.g., number of contacts, fuel pressurization cycles, flight hours in AR environment) are specified and documented in flight and maintenance manuals. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Examination of requirement specifications and design documentation identify service life requirements, life-limited part definitions and plan for tracking life-limited components.
(2) Examination of draft maintenance manuals and maintenance plans verifies LLP replacement instructions are documented. Analysis.
  (1) Fatigue analysis verifies that the AR system meets the required service life and identifies life-limited AR components. Test.
    (1) Lab test: System endurance testing verifies AR system meets service life requirements. Qualification testing in a laboratory environment verifies component life and durability performance in expected environment.
    (2) Ground test: Ground testing verifies load spectrum and usage are aligned with the analytically developed fatigue load spectrum. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Examination.
    (3) Examination of maintenance and flight manuals verify life-limited AR components are tracked and replacement intervals identified. Test.
(3) Flight test: Flight testing verifies load spectrum and usage are aligned with the analytically developed fatigue load spectrum.
